text:
alex: Hey team — quick ping. PR #41827 landed some client-side cache header wiring that touches routing decisions in the runtime. @runtime @security @infra can you take a quick look? Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/pull/41827

Diff touches:
- runtime router decision (routing.go)
- platform cache-control header wiring (frontend/handler.go)
- infra ALB annotations for stickiness (k8s/ingress.yaml)

CI: local unit tests pass but canary e2e is flaky for this.

Here is the server response that failed on the canary: 
```bash
# canary curl
curl -i -H 'Host: canary.app.redwood' https://10.2.3.4/health
HTTP/2 503
x-runtime-error: kvcache-miss
```

I plan to hold merge until runtime + security sign off and infra confirms no routing change required. Can we get eyes in the next ~2h?

priya: @alex quick q — does this change the default cache TTL? I skimmed the diff and saw 0 -> 60s in the frontend handler.

mike: I'll take runtime first pass. If it's just header plumbing should be low risk. pinging @jordan for perf/regression checks.

jordan: saw something similar in perf runs yesterday, will re-run the workloads against the canary image. ETA ~30m.

sarah: Security — I'll need the full request/response headers for the failing case, and confirmation this doesn't leak any auth cookies. can you paste raw headers?

alex: pasted below, redacted cookie values:
```
:method: GET
:scheme: https
:authority: canary.app.redwood
accept: */*
cache-control: no-cache
cookie: __session_redacted
x-forwarded-for: 10.1.2.3
x-runtime-error: kvcache-miss
```
No auth tokens in headers besides the session cookie (server-only).

infra-bot: CI pipeline status: canary-e2e flaky_tests=1, network-policy=failing, rollout=blocked.

mike: runtime note — router fallback path currently returns 503 on kvcache-miss; we should fallback to the cold-read path instead. PR looks like it inadvertently removed the fallback for gRPC proxied requests. I'll open a tiny follow-up to reintroduce fallback and add a regression test; tagging @alex.

alex: thanks — please link the follow-up PR. if runtime can do the fallback fix we can merge both in the same canary window.

jordan: perf runs complete — ~<10% p95 increase when kvcache-miss is forced on small workloads. not great but acceptable if fallback reduces the 503 surface.

sarah: Security can approve conditionally — fallback reintroduced + a regression test for cookie handling. after that :shipit:.

mike: created PR #41828 to reintroduce fallback and test it: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/pull/41828

alex: cool. i'll block the main PR until #41828 is merged and canary QA green. thanks all.

jordan: will re-run perf after fallback PR merges and post numbers.

priya: thx — i'll schedule a short canary window (45m) and update the release board.

mike: noted, will shepherd runtime side.

sarah: will do final security signoff once tests pass.

alex: ack, appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
